user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot fusion be made inductive — scoring each image on its own, without the test-set min-max normalisation of the released code — without losing AUROC, and does this give a threshold that transfers to unseen modalities? The inductive fusion standardises each branch with leave-one-out statistics of the K normal support images (each support's zero-shot map, and its few-shot map against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports, pooled over patches and levels), adds the standardised branches, and pools the fused map with the mean of its top 2% pixels; the threshold is the 95th percentile of the supports' leave-one-out image scores. Primary outcome: image- and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive fusion on every held-out modality and K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the transductive AUROC across random test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Secondary outcomes: sensitivity, realised specificity, F1 and expected calibration error at the support-derived threshold. We also record whether the few-shot baselines compared in the target paper (APRIL-GAN, WinCLIP) normalise over the test set in their public code, to judge how widely the finding applies.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Bounded leave-one-out z-score fusion (LOO-Z) for per-image MVFA scoring
SUMMARY: Standardise MVFA's zero-shot and few-shot maps with leave-one-out statistics of the K support normals, clip them to a bounded range, fuse with inverse-variance weights and pool the top 2% pixels, so every image is scored on its own.
HYPOTHESIS: On held-out BMAD modalities with K >= 4, LOO-Z fusion achieves image- and pixel-level AUROC within 1 point of MVFA's transductive fusion while its AUROC varies at least 3x less across random 50% test subsamples and 10%/50% prevalence resamples, and its support-derived threshold yields realised specificity within 5 points of the nominal 95%.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: the fusion rule (transductive test-set min-max + 0.5 sum vs. LOO-Z). LOO-Z computes, for each branch b in {zero, few} and level l, the mean and standard deviation of patch scores of the K support normals, where the few-shot score of support i is computed against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports (leave-one-out) and the zero-shot score uses the text anchors as usual. Each test patch score is converted to z = (s - mu_bl)/sigma_bl, clipped to [-3, 6] (bounded drift), summed over levels, and the two branches are combined with weights w_b proportional to 1/Var(LOO image scores of branch b). The image score is the mean of the top 2% fused pixels. Dependent variables: image-/pixel-level AUROC, sensitivity/specificity/F1 at the threshold tau = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores, ECE of the logistic-mapped score, and the stability of AUROC under test-set subsampling and prevalence shift.
RATIONALE: The chain moves from MVFA's transductive fusion (test-set min-max, fixed 0.5) to methods that score each image against references only (MadCLIP) and that bound how far a per-image adjustment can move (ReCAP). The missing step for MVFA is to replace test-set statistics with reference statistics from the K normal supports and to bound each branch's contribution so neither dominates, which yields a deployable per-image score and a threshold that can be set before seeing target labels.
METHOD: 1) test_few.py: refactor scoring into score_image(x, supports) that never touches other test images. 2) Support statistics (new function support_stats in utils.py): for each support normal i, build memory banks from the other K-1 supports at each level l (det and seg tokens as in MVFA), compute few-shot patch scores 1 - max cos; compute zero-shot patch scores softmax(100 * f_l @ T)[abnormal]; store mu_bl, sigma_bl (sigma floored at 1e-3) and the LOO image scores. For K=2 the LOO bank contains a single image; statistics are pooled over all 289 patches x 4 levels so they remain defined. 3) For a test image: z_bl = clip((s_bl - mu_bl)/sigma_bl, -3, 6); Z_b = sum_l z_bl upsampled to 240x240; F = w_zero Z_zero + w_few Z_few with w_b = (1/v_b)/(1/v_zero + 1/v_few), v_b the variance of branch b's LOO image scores. 4) Image score = mean of top 2% of F (about 1,150 of 57,600 pixels; ablations: max, mean, top 1%, top 5%). 5) Threshold tau = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores; probability via Platt mapping fitted on support LOO scores with pseudo-negatives only is not identifiable, so ECE is computed after mapping p = sigmoid((score - tau)/s) with s = support score IQR. 6) No training changes; reuse MVFA checkpoints trained under the shared protocol.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: MVFA transductive fusion (released code); MVFA with per-image fusion but no normalisation (raw sum); LOO-Z without clipping; LOO-Z with equal weights. Ablations: aggregation operator; K. Metrics: image AUROC, pixel AUROC, PRO; sensitivity, specificity, F1 at tau; ECE; AUROC standard deviation over 20 random 50% test subsamples and under prevalence resampling to 10% and 50% abnormal. Falsification: if LOO-Z loses more than 2 AUROC points on average, or its AUROC is not more stable than the transductive fusion, the hypothesis is rejected.

Idea B:
TITLE: Episode-calibrated weighted Fisher fusion: learning per-level weights of support p-values on source-modality episodes
SUMMARY: Compute per-level, per-branch empirical p-values against the target's support normals (inductive, distribution-free) and combine them with weights and a logistic mapping learned on simulated K-shot episodes from the source modalities' labelled validation images.
HYPOTHESIS: Weighted Fisher fusion with episode-learned level/branch weights improves image AUROC by at least 1 point and reduces expected calibration error by at least 25% relative to unweighted Fisher fusion on held-out BMAD modalities for K >= 4, without any target labels.
RATIONALE: Parent 1 (Fisher) gives every level and branch equal weight although the reviews and MVFA's own ablations suggest levels differ in usefulness; parent 2 (episode calibrator) learns from real source abnormal images but on hand-chosen features. Using the eight -log p terms (4 levels x 2 branches) as the calibrator's features keeps Fisher's distribution-free, support-anchored inputs and lets real labelled source data decide how much each level and branch should count. Because the inputs are p-values relative to each episode's own supports, they are on the same scale across modalities, which addresses the reviewers' concern about cross-modality transfer of the calibrator.
METHOD: 1) Episodes: for each source modality, 200 episodes of K normal supports (valid/good) and 64 balanced validation images. 2) For each image, features x = [mean of top-2% of -log p_bl over pixels] for b in {zero, few}, l in 1..4 (8 features), p from LOO support nulls as in Fisher-MVFA. 3) Logistic regression with non-negative weights (projected gradient), L2 = 1.0, pooled over source episodes. 4) Target: same features with the target supports; probability p = sigma(w^T x + b); threshold at p = 0.5 and at the 95% support-specificity point. 5) Code: train_calibrator.py (episodes), scoring.py fisher_features(); no adapter retraining.
EXPERIMENT: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: unweighted Fisher; episode calibrator on raw score features; LOO-Z. Ablations: non-negativity constraint; per-level vs per-branch weights only. Metrics: AUROC, ECE, Brier, sensitivity/specificity at both thresholds; learned weights per held-out fold (interpretability). Falsification: no AUROC or ECE gain over unweighted Fisher.
